definitionEn: a strong wish to achieve something important in your life or career
situation: You talk about what someone hopes to achieve in their career or life, often something ambitious.

examples.text: The survey asked teenagers about their career [[aspirations]] and their fears about the future.
The new mayor promised to listen to the [[aspirations]] of young families who can't afford homes.
Her lifelong [[aspiration]] to run her own restaurant finally came true last year.

texts: Many graduates have no clear [[aspirations]] yet.
The novel explores the hopes and [[aspirations]] of immigrant families.
Parents often project their own [[aspirations]] onto their children.

badCollocation.noteRu: Aspiration — серьёзная жизненная цель (карьера, образование). О желании что-то купить говорят want: I want to buy new shoes.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Осуществить стремления — fulfil (или realise, achieve) your aspirations. Execute и perform — про задачи и действия, complete — про работу.

nuance.text: Her [[aspiration]] is to open a small bakery by the sea.
nuance.explanationRu: Aspiration — то, к чему вы стремитесь, ваша цель. Inspiration — вдохновение, то, что подталкивает к творчеству. Мечта открыть пекарню — это aspiration.

reverse.text: The painter found [[inspiration]] in the landscapes of her childhood.
reverse.explanationRu: Источник творческих идей — inspiration. Aspiration — цель, к которой стремишься; её не «находят в пейзажах».

fixIt.text: She has serious [[pretensions]] to become a professional singer.
fixIt.explanationRu: Стремление стать кем-то — aspirations. Pretensions — ложный друг русского «претензии»: это «притязания, претенциозность».

wordFormation.text: The charity works to raise the [[aspirations]] of children from poor families.

reply.context: At a job interview, you're asked: "Where do you see yourself in five years?"
options: My aspiration is that I was born in a small town near Kazan.
Aspirations? No idea, mate — whatever happens, happens.
My aspiration is to lead a small team and help shape the product.
reply.explanationRu: Aspiration — цель на будущее, поэтому подходит третий ответ. Место рождения — факт из прошлого, а не стремление. Второй ответ слишком фамильярный для собеседования.

definitionEn: to have a strong wish to achieve something or to become a particular kind of person
situation: Someone has a big goal, such as becoming a writer or a manager, and hopes to reach it one day.

examples.text: Like many young actors, she [[aspired]] to work in film rather than theatre.
Anyone who [[aspires]] to a management role needs strong people skills.
The programme helps students from poor areas [[aspire]] to careers in medicine and law.

texts: Most young musicians [[aspire]] to play in a major orchestra.
We [[aspire]] to be the most trusted bank in the region.
What kind of life do you [[aspire]] to?

badCollocation.noteRu: Aspire не бывает переходным: aspire to a promotion, aspire to become a manager.

collocationTask.prompt: She aspires ___ a career in law
collocationTask.explanationRu: Aspire всегда с предлогом to: aspire to a career, aspire to become. At, on и in с этим глаголом не используются.

nuance.text: She [[aspires]] to a senior position within the next five years.
nuance.explanationRu: Русское «претендовать на должность» — aspire to (или apply for) a position. Pretend — ложный друг: это «притворяться».

reverse.text: He [[pretended]] to be asleep when his boss called.
reverse.explanationRu: Притворяться — pretend. Aspire значит «стремиться к цели», к притворству оно отношения не имеет.

fixIt.text: As a teenager, he [[inspired]] to play for the national team.
fixIt.explanationRu: Стремиться к цели — aspire to do something. Inspire — «вдохновлять кого-то»: The coach inspired him to play.

wordFormation.text: The workshop is open to all [[aspiring]] writers, whatever their age.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Do you want to be a manager one day?"
options: Not really — I aspire to be great at what I do, not to manage people.
Not really — I aspire my manager every day, and that's enough.
Negative. Managerial positions are not that to which I aspire.
reply.explanationRu: Aspire to be — «стремиться быть». Во втором ответе aspire употреблено как «восхищаться» (это admire) и без to. Третий звучит канцелярски для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: She has always dreamed of becoming a judge.
rewrite.explanationRu: Aspire to do something — стремиться, мечтать стать кем-то.

definitionEn: the crime of attacking someone physically, or an act of this kind
senseNote: Выбрано значение «нападение на человека (преступление)»; ещё бывает военный штурм и переносное «атака на права».
situation: Someone is accused in court of hitting or physically attacking another person.

examples.text: He was arrested and charged with [[assault]] after a fight outside a bar.
Hospitals report that [[assaults]] on nurses and doctors have risen sharply this year.
The footballer was cleared of [[assault]] after the video showed he never touched the fan.

texts: She was the victim of a serious [[assault]] last year.
Two men will stand trial for [[assault]] next month.
Any [[assault]] on staff will be reported to the police.

badCollocation.noteRu: С assault не говорят do: нужно commit an assault, а в суде — be charged with assault.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Обвинение в нападении — be charged with assault. Attack, aggression и violence в юридическом языке так не используются: это не названия статей.

nuance.text: The man was found guilty of [[assault]] and given six months in prison.
nuance.explanationRu: Assault — юридическое название преступления «нападение, побои». Attack — нападение вообще, но не статья закона: guilty of assault, а не of attack.

reverse.text: My uncle had a heart [[attack]] while he was playing tennis.
reverse.explanationRu: Сердечный приступ — heart attack. Assault — нападение одного человека на другого, к болезни не относится.

fixIt.text: The driver was charged with [[aggression]] after he punched a cyclist.
fixIt.explanationRu: Статья за нападение — assault: be charged with assault. Aggression — агрессивное поведение, а не название преступления.

definitionEn: to bring people or things together in one place, or to gather as a group
senseNote: Выбрано значение «собирать людей или сведения вместе», а не «собирать мебель или механизм из деталей».
situation: A leader brings experts together into a team, or a crowd of people gathers in one place.

examples.text: The director [[assembled]] a team of top engineers to design the new bridge.
By nine o'clock, a small crowd had [[assembled]] outside the court.
It took the journalist two years to [[assemble]] enough evidence to publish the story.

texts: Journalists [[assembled]] outside the hotel, waiting for news.
She [[assembled]] a small but loyal team.
The museum has [[assembled]] a remarkable collection of Roman coins.

badCollocation.noteRu: Деньги на подарок collect (или raise), а не assemble. Assemble — собирать людей, команду, доказательства.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Собрать команду — assemble (или put together) a team. Collect — собирать вещи или забирать кого-то, compose — сочинять, accumulate — накапливать.

nuance.text: The coach [[assembled]] a strong squad of young players for the tournament.
nuance.explanationRu: Собрать команду из людей — assemble. Collect — собирать предметы (марки, мусор) или забирать кого-то (collect the kids from school); collected a squad звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: Could you [[collect]] the kids from school today?
reverse.explanationRu: Забрать детей из школы — collect. Assemble — собрать людей в группу или команду, а не забрать кого-то.

fixIt.text: The government has [[composed]] a team of experts to investigate the crash.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Собрать команду» — assemble a team. Compose значит «сочинять» (музыку, текст), а «составить команду» так не переводится.

wordFormation.text: The constitution guarantees freedom of speech and freedom of [[assembly]].

reply.context: Your manager says: "We need to launch the app in three months. Can we do it?"
options: Only if we assemble the deadline and make it a bit longer.
Only if we assemble a small team right now and give them full control.
Affirmative; a team shall be assembled forthwith, in accordance with your wishes.
reply.explanationRu: Assemble a team — собрать команду, это естественный ответ. Срок (deadline) не assemble, его переносят (extend). Третий вариант звучит как старинный приказ.

rewrite.original: About two hundred people gathered outside the town hall.
rewrite.frame: A crowd of about two hundred people ____ outside the town hall.
rewrite.explanationRu: Assemble — собраться вместе (о толпе, группе людей).

definitionEn: a group of people elected to make laws or decisions for a country or region
senseNote: Выбрано значение «выборный орган власти» (National Assembly), а не школьная линейка или сборка деталей.
situation: Elected representatives meet regularly to debate and vote on new laws for their country or region.

examples.text: The regional [[assembly]] voted to ban single-use plastic bags from next year.
In history class we learned how the country's first elected [[assembly]] was formed.
My cousin works as an adviser to a member of the national [[assembly]].

texts: The [[assembly]] meets every Tuesday and Thursday.
She was elected to the [[assembly]] at just twenty-six.
The bill was rejected by the [[assembly]] after a long debate.

badCollocation.noteRu: Собрание акционеров — a shareholders' meeting или annual general meeting. Assembly — выборный законодательный орган.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Избраться в региональный парламент — be elected to the regional assembly. Meeting — встреча, gathering — сборище, audience — зрители; туда не избирают.

nuance.text: The national [[assembly]] passed the new law by 210 votes to 95.
nuance.explanationRu: Assembly — выборный орган, который принимает законы. Meeting — любое собрание или встреча, например совещание на работе; законы на нём не принимают.

reverse.text: We have a team [[meeting]] every Monday at ten.
reverse.explanationRu: Рабочее совещание — meeting. Assembly в этом значении — парламент или выборный орган, а не встреча коллег.

fixIt.text: Members of the regional [[gathering]] voted against the new tax.
fixIt.explanationRu: Выборный орган, который голосует за налоги, — assembly. Gathering — просто сборище людей, встреча.

definitionEn: to state firmly and confidently that something is true
senseNote: Выбрано значение «твёрдо утверждать»; assert yourself («проявить твёрдость») — отдельное значение.
situation: Someone states strongly that a claim is true, often in a debate, an article or in court.

examples.text: The company [[asserts]] that its products are completely safe, despite several complaints.
In her essay, she [[asserted]] that social media had made politics more extreme.
Throughout the trial, he has continued to [[assert]] his innocence.

texts: The author [[asserted]] that the painting was a fake.
Several witnesses [[asserted]] that the driver had been speeding.
The report [[asserted]] that prices would fall, but they rose.

badCollocation.noteRu: Утвердить бюджет — approve the budget. Assert — «утверждать, заявлять», что что-то правда; путаница из-за русского «утверждать/утвердить».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Настаивать на своей невиновности — assert (или maintain) your innocence. Confess и admit — про признание вины, approve — «одобрять».

nuance.text: In court, the witness [[asserted]] that she had never met the defendant.
nuance.explanationRu: Assert — твёрдо заявлять, что что-то правда. Assure — заверять кого-то, чтобы успокоить, и требует дополнения: assure the court that. Без него assured здесь неверно.

reverse.text: The pilot [[assured]] the passengers that there was no danger.
reverse.explanationRu: Успокоить людей обещанием — assure somebody that. Assert не принимает дополнение-человека: asserted the passengers — ошибка.

fixIt.text: He [[approves]] that he was at home all evening, but nobody believes him.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Он утверждает, что» — he asserts (или claims) that. Approve — «одобрять, утверждать документ»: approve a plan.

wordFormation.text: Since becoming a manager, she has learned to be more [[assertive]] in meetings.

reply.context: In a seminar, a classmate asks: "The article says remote workers are less productive. Is that true?"
options: The author asserted the article to the editor last week.
I would hereby assert that the aforementioned claim lacks empirical grounding.
The author asserts it, but she doesn't give any real data to support it.
reply.explanationRu: Assert — твёрдо заявлять, что что-то правда, часто без доказательств. Статью редактору не assert, а send или submit. Второй ответ слишком напыщенный для разговора с однокурсником.

rewrite.original: The minister said firmly that the figures were correct.
rewrite.frame: The minister ____ the figures were correct.
rewrite.explanationRu: Assert that — твёрдо заявить, что что-то правда.

definitionEn: a statement that something is true, made firmly and often without proof
situation: Someone states firmly that something is true, and others question whether there is any evidence for it.

examples.text: Several scientists have challenged her [[assertion]] that the drug has no side effects.
The manager's [[assertion]] that the project was on schedule turned out to be false.
There is no evidence for the widely repeated [[assertion]] that we only use 10% of our brains.

texts: Her [[assertion]] was not supported by any facts.
I strongly disagree with the [[assertion]] that money brings happiness.
The judge rejected the lawyer's [[assertion]] as pure speculation.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Сделать утверждение» — make an assertion, а не do.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Подтвердить утверждение доказательствами — support (или back up) an assertion. Carry, keep и lift с assertion не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Critics dismissed the author's [[assertion]] that grammar no longer matters.
nuance.explanationRu: Assertion — заявление, что что-то правда, часто спорное. Assurance — заверение, которое дают кому-то, чтобы успокоить; мнение автора о грамматике не assurance.

reverse.text: The bank gave us its [[assurance]] that our savings were safe.
reverse.explanationRu: Заверение, данное клиентам, чтобы их успокоить, — assurance. Assertion — просто твёрдое заявление, его не «дают» кому-то.

fixIt.text: Few experts accept the minister's [[approval]] that the economy has fully recovered.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «утверждение» в смысле «заявление» — assertion. Approval — «одобрение, утверждение документа»: approval of the budget.

wordFormation.text: His [[assertion]] that he had never been to Paris was quickly proved false.

definitionEn: a promise or firm statement that something is true or will happen, meant to remove doubt
senseNote: Выбрано значение «заверение, гарантия»; в британском английском assurance бывает и «страхование жизни», а self-assurance — «уверенность в себе».
situation: Someone promises you that something will definitely happen, so that you stop worrying about it.

examples.text: The minister gave an [[assurance]] that no jobs would be lost at the factory.
Despite repeated [[assurances]] from the landlord, the heating still doesn't work.
Before signing, the client wanted some [[assurance]] that the software would be delivered on time.

texts: Can you give me your [[assurance]] that this won't happen again?
Voters want [[assurance]] that their personal data is safe.
He received a written [[assurance]] from the bank.

badCollocation.noteRu: Заверение дают и получают: give an assurance, receive (или get) an assurance. Калька «взять обещание» — take — здесь не работает.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ an assurance that no jobs will be lost
collocationTask.explanationRu: Дать заверение — give (или provide) an assurance. Say и tell не сочетаются с этим существительным, а do здесь вообще не подходит.

nuance.text: Despite [[assurances]] from the airline that the plane was safe, many passengers refused to board.
nuance.explanationRu: Assurance — заверение, обещание, что всё будет хорошо. Insurance — страховка, договор со страховой компанией; ею пассажиров не успокаивают перед посадкой.

reverse.text: Don't forget to buy travel [[insurance]] before your trip.
reverse.explanationRu: Туристическая страховка — travel insurance. Assurance как «страхование» встречается только в британском life assurance, в остальных случаях это «заверение».

fixIt.text: The manager gave us his personal [[warranty]] that the problem would be fixed by Friday.
fixIt.explanationRu: Личное обещание, чтобы нас успокоить, — assurance. Warranty — гарантия на товар (two-year warranty), а не слово человека.

wordFormation.text: We have received an [[assurance]] from the builders that the work will be finished in May.

reply.context: An email from a client asks: "Can you guarantee the order will arrive before the conference?"
options: Yeah, no worries, total assurance, mate!
I can give you my personal assurance that it will be delivered by Tuesday.
Yes — we've bought assurance for the conference, so everything is covered.
reply.explanationRu: Give someone your assurance — дать слово, заверить. В третьем ответе assurance спутано со страховкой (insurance), а первый слишком фамильярный для письма клиенту.

definitionEn: protection that a country gives to people who have fled danger in their own country
senseNote: Выбрано значение «политическое убежище»; устаревшее значение «психиатрическая лечебница» здесь не рассматривается.
situation: A person who faces persecution at home asks another country for legal protection and permission to stay.

examples.text: After receiving threats at home, the journalist applied for [[asylum]] in Canada.
Thousands of people who fled the war are still waiting to be granted [[asylum]].
During the war, the famous painter was given [[asylum]] by a neutral country.

texts: He was granted [[asylum]] after a long legal battle.
The family is seeking [[asylum]] in Germany.
Her [[asylum]] application was finally approved in March.

badCollocation.text: give [[asylum]] to a homeless man for the night
badCollocation.noteRu: Приютить бездомного — give someone shelter. Asylum — политическое убежище, которое даёт государство.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Политическое убежище — political asylum. Shelter — приют или укрытие, housing — жильё, hiding — «укрытие, прятки».

nuance.text: The opposition leader applied for [[asylum]] at the embassy.
nuance.explanationRu: Asylum — официальный статус, о нём подают заявление: apply for asylum. Refuge — укрытие от опасности, его «находят» (take refuge), а не оформляют.

reverse.text: During the storm, the hikers took [[refuge]] in a mountain hut.
reverse.explanationRu: Укрыться от бури — take refuge. Asylum — юридическая защита, которую даёт государство, а не укрытие в хижине.

fixIt.text: The court ruled that she should be given political [[shelter]] in the UK.
fixIt.explanationRu: Политическое убежище — political asylum. Shelter — укрытие или приют (a homeless shelter), а не правовой статус.

definitionEn: creating a strong mood or feeling, often mysterious, romantic or exciting
senseNote: Выбрано значение «создающий особое настроение» (о музыке, фильме, месте), а не научное «атмосферный» (atmospheric pressure).
situation: You describe music, a film, a photo or a place that creates a special, often mysterious or romantic feeling.

examples.text: The film's [[atmospheric]] soundtrack, all low strings and distant bells, makes every scene feel haunted.
We had dinner in a tiny, [[atmospheric]] restaurant lit only by candles.
Her [[atmospheric]] black-and-white photos of foggy streets have won several prizes.

texts: The old castle is wonderfully [[atmospheric]] at night.
Their new album is dark, slow and very [[atmospheric]].
The novel opens with an [[atmospheric]] description of a winter village.

badCollocation.noteRu: Atmospheric описывает места, музыку, фильмы и свет, но не людей. О человеке скажут charismatic или charming.

collocationTask.prompt: an ___ little café lit by candles
collocationTask.explanationRu: Место с особым настроением — an atmospheric café. Atmosphere — существительное, emotional описывает чувства людей, athletic — «спортивный».

nuance.text: The ruined abbey, wrapped in fog, looked wonderfully [[atmospheric]].
nuance.explanationRu: Atmospheric — место, музыка или фильм создают настроение. Emotional — о людях и их чувствах или о трогательном событии; руины не бывают emotional.

reverse.text: The wedding speech was so [[emotional]] that half the guests were crying.
reverse.explanationRu: Трогательная речь, от которой плачут, — emotional. Atmospheric описывает обстановку и настроение места, а не силу чувств.

fixIt.text: The director uses fog and silence to create a very [[atmosphere]] opening scene.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед существительным scene нужно прилагательное: a very atmospheric scene. Atmosphere — существительное.

wordFormation.text: Candles and old jazz records give the bar a wonderfully [[atmospheric]] feel.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Where should we go for our anniversary dinner?"
options: There's a very atmospheric place near the airport — the air there is really fresh.
I propose an establishment of considerable atmospheric merit.
There's an atmospheric little place by the river — candles, brick walls, live piano.
reply.explanationRu: Atmospheric — место с особым настроением: свечи, кирпич, живая музыка. Свежий воздух тут ни при чём, а второй ответ звучит слишком чопорно для разговора с другом.
